seoTitle: Free Base32 Encode and Decode Online (RFC 4648)
metaDescription: Encode UTF-8 text to Base32 or decode it back, using the standard RFC 4648 alphabet or the extended hex one, with optional padding. Free, in your browser.
intro: Encode text as Base32 or decode a Base32 string back to text. Choose the standard alphabet or the extended hex alphabet, and switch padding on or off.
why:
Base32 is what you find in two-factor setup keys, some file hashes, onion addresses and case-insensitive identifiers. Its letters and digits 2 to 7 avoid easily confused characters, so a person can read it out loud or type it from a printout.

This tool follows RFC 4648. It encodes your text as UTF-8 bytes, writes them in groups of five bits, and pads with = if you want. Decoding is case-insensitive and skips spaces and padding. When a character does not belong to the chosen alphabet you get an error naming it, which is the usual sign of a typo or of the wrong alphabet.
howTo: Choose the direction: encode or decode.
Paste your text, or the Base32 string, into the Input box.
Tick "Extended hex alphabet" if your data uses the Base32hex variant, and untick Padding if you do not want = signs.

faq.q: Why would I use Base32 instead of Base64?
faq.a: Base32 uses only uppercase letters and digits, so it survives case-insensitive systems and is easier to read aloud. The price is size: it is about 60 percent longer than the original data, against 33 percent for Base64.

faq.q: What is the extended hex alphabet?
faq.a: It is the Base32hex variant from RFC 4648, which uses 0-9 and A-V so that encoded values keep the same sort order as the raw bytes. Most applications use the standard A-Z and 2-7 alphabet instead.

faq.q: Can I decode a two-factor setup key?
faq.a: Technically yes, since those keys are Base32. But the decoded bytes are a binary secret, not text, and you will usually just see an error that they are not valid UTF-8. Do not paste real authenticator secrets into pages you do not trust.
Yes. Decoding converts to uppercase first and ignores spaces and = padding, so keys copied with spaces for readability still decode.
